children: is seeking workers for about 500 open positions in the United States as the Canadian business-jet manufacturer faces a possible ban on selling aircraft in the country. The vacancies include jobs at a new service center in Fort Wayne, Indiana, scheduled to open in mid-November, Reuters reported Wednesday.

For investors, the dispute creates a significant policy risk because the United States generates roughly half of Bombardier’s sales. A ban or new tariffs could hurt deliveries, revenue and profit margins. However, the company’s continuing expansion in the United States and support from lawmakers in states where it employs workers may strengthen its position in negotiations.

Bombardier aircraft can still be delivered to American customers. Aerospace also was excluded from the latest U.S. retaliatory measures against Canada, although the White House is considering additional action involving the company.

President Donald Trump has threatened to block Bombardier from the U.S. market unless it manufactures aircraft in the country. The pressure comes despite the restoration last year of a longstanding agreement allowing airplanes and components to cross the border without tariffs.

Republican senators from Kansas, where Bombardier employs about 1,500 people, have urged the administration to consider the company’s economic contribution. The dispute adds another source of uncertainty to U.S.-Canada trade relations ahead of the November midterm elections.

title: Bombardier presses ahead with U.S. hiring despite Trump threat
